quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #4
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: You miss your exit on a freeway. What should you do?

options.text: Turn quickly from your current lane.
Keep driving until the next exit or safe place to turn around.
Signal other drivers to stop so you can turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep driving until the next exit or safe place to turn around.
questions.explanation: If you miss your exit, do not back up. Go to the next exit or turn where you can safely turn around. Backing up on a freeway or shoulder is illegal.

questions.question: When you see a railroad crossing ahead, you should:
questions.explanation: When you see a railroad crossing sign, slow down, look for a train, and be ready to stop. If red lights are flashing or the gate is down, stop 15 to 50 feet before the tracks. Do not try to go around the gate.

questions.question: Drinking alcohol while driving is:

options.text: Safe if you drink only a little.

questions.explanation: Drinking and driving is a serious safety problem. You cannot drive safely after drinking alcohol or taking drugs. It puts you and others at risk.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black symbols on a yellow background. They alert you to hazards ahead. This sign warns you of an upcoming steep hill. Slow down and adjust your speed to drive safely.

questions.question: You cannot pass another vehicle:
questions.explanation: It is illegal and unsafe to pass on hills, curves, at intersections, and at railroad crossings.

questions.question: When you see a red traffic light, you should:

options.text: Drive through if no other cars are coming.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is watching.

questions.explanation: You must come to a complete stop at a red light. Running a red light is illegal and dangerous. You may turn right on a red light only if there is no sign that says you cannot.

questions.question: A seat belt should be adjusted so that it:

options.text: Fits snugly across your hip bones and lower belly.
Stops the seat belt alarm from going off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fits snugly across your hip bones and lower belly.
questions.explanation: The lap belt should fit snugly across your hip bones and lower belly. The shoulder belt should be comfortable so you can fit your fist between it and your chest.

questions.question: In a crash, the best protection is:

options.text: Only a lap and shoulder belt.
Both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag.
questions.explanation: Seat belts can double your chance of surviving a crash and greatly reduce serious injury. Airbags work best with seat belts in a front-end crash. Always wear both your shoulder and lap belts.

questions.question: When can you have an open alcohol container in a vehicle?

options.text: While the vehicle is being driven.

questions.explanation: It is always illegal to have an open alcohol container in a vehicle on a public road. This is true whether the vehicle is stopped, parked, or being driven. Breaking this law can result in a fine up to $500.

questions.question: Stress can affect your driving by:

options.text: Making it hard to focus on driving.
Reducing your chance of an accident.
Making you more alert to others around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Making it hard to focus on driving.
questions.explanation: Strong emotions can hurt your driving ability. If you feel worried, excited, afraid, angry, or sad, you may not drive well. Stress reduces your concentration. It is better to wait before driving than to risk driving when emotionally upset.

questions.question: If you pass your exit on the interstate, what should you do?

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Make a U-turn to go back to the exit.
Continue driving and use the next exit.
Put your vehicle in reverse to go back to the exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving and use the next exit.
questions.explanation: Do not make a sudden turn at your exit. If you miss your exit, drive to the next one.

questions.question: Can you park directly across the street from a fire station entrance?

options.text: Yes, if the emergency vehicles just left the station.

questions.explanation: You cannot park within 20 feet of a fire station entrance on the same side of the road. You cannot park within 75 feet of the entrance on the opposite side of the road. Parked cars can cause accidents.

questions.question: What is the purpose of highway markings?

options.text: They are only found in construction zones.
They are usually red and blue in color.

questions.explanation: Highway markings help drivers position their vehicles correctly. They show safe passing zones and warn drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: What can cause distracted driving?

options.text: Talking or texting on a cell phone.
Changing a radio station or CD.

questions.explanation: Drivers make about 200 decisions for every mile driven. You must focus all your attention on driving. Any other activity can be dangerous.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: You must come to a complete stop.
Drive with caution and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: An eight-sided sign always means stop. Come to a complete stop and wait for any vehicles or pedestrians to clear before going.

questions.question: What happens if you drink alcohol while taking prescription or over-the-counter medicine?

options.text: The medicine reduces the effect of the alcohol.
The alcohol helps the medicine work better.
The effects of the alcohol or medicine can be multiplied.
There is no effect because they are different.

questions.correctAnswerText: The effects of the alcohol or medicine can be multiplied.
questions.explanation: Drinking alcohol with other drugs increases how much both affect you. For example, one drink with cold medicine can affect you like several drinks without medicine.

questions.question: When should you slow down and increase your following distance?

options.text: When you cannot see far ahead.

questions.explanation: Slow down and increase your following distance when roads are wet, traffic is heavy, or your vision is limited. You must always be able to stop within the distance you can see ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that bicycles may be in the area ahead.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right.

questions.question: Where should you stop your car when approaching a stop line?

options.text: On top of the stop line.

questions.explanation: Stop lines are painted on the road to create a safe walking space for pedestrians in front of stopped cars. Stop before the painted line.

questions.question: When approaching railroad tracks, what should you do?

options.text: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
Speed up to cross before the gate lowers.
Ignore how many tracks you need to cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: When approaching railroad tracks, look and listen for trains. Slow down and be ready to stop if a train or other vehicle is using the tracks.

questions.question: What can happen when you mix alcohol with another drug?

options.text: Only the alcohol effect gets weaker.

questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol and another drug can make both effects stronger. For example, one drink while taking cold medicine might feel like several drinks.

questions.question: When turning or changing lanes, you must:

options.text: Always signal, even if no other cars are near.
Signal only if other cars are nearby.
Signal only in heavy nighttime traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always signal, even if no other cars are near.
questions.explanation: Always signal when changing lanes, turning, or pulling from a curb. Do not get lazy and skip this important law.

questions.question: Before entering a roundabout, you must slow down and yield to:
questions.explanation: When entering a roundabout, yield to all pedestrians, bicycles, and cars already in it.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Tiredness while driving is as dangerous as driving under the influence. If you feel tired, stop driving.

questions.question: A person using a white cane or guide dog is most likely:
questions.explanation: You must always yield to a blind person using a white cane or guide dog.

questions.question: When leaving a parking space, you should:

options.text: Look around for children and objects in the way.

questions.explanation: Check all mirrors and look around your car for children or other obstacles. Signal other drivers that you are leaving your spot.

questions.question: Mixing alcohol with drugs can:
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol and drugs can strengthen the effects of both. Driving is unsafe after alcohol or drugs, and even more dangerous when they are mixed.

questions.question: If a large truck is passing you, what should you do?

options.text: Make it harder for the truck to pass.

questions.explanation: Help the truck driver by staying to the far side of your lane and slightly slowing down. This makes it easier for the truck to pass safely. Do not speed up while being passed.

questions.question: A driver entering a public road from a driveway or private road:

options.text: Must yield to drivers already on the public road.
Can force their way into traffic.
Can assume other drivers will move for them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must yield to drivers already on the public road.
questions.explanation: When entering a public road from a driveway or private road, yield to all drivers already on the public road. Merge safely when it is possible to do so.
